message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the two orders **Carnivora** (to which lions belong) and **Perissodactyla** (to which zebras belong).  
That ancestor was a small, probably insectivorous placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, before the two lineages diverged into the distinct families Felidae and Equidae.
